title: Decimal detective: rational or irrational?
summary: Watch the digits of a number: stops or repeats means rational, neither means irrational.
alt: Decimal digits of {{if n==0 | 3/4 | the chosen number}} with the repeating block highlighted.

shapes.text: it never ends and no block repeats

steps.title: Every number has a decimal
steps.narration: Every real number can be written as a **decimal**. Use the buttons to pick a number and watch its digits. We start with \( \frac{3}{4} \): divide 3 by 4.

steps.title: It stops: terminating
steps.narration: \( \frac{3}{4} = 0.75 \). After the 5 only zeros follow, so the decimal **terminates**. Every terminating decimal is a [[rat|rational]] number.

steps.title: It repeats: recurring
steps.narration: \( \frac{1}{3} = 0.333\ldots \) never stops, but one digit **repeats** again and again. A recurring decimal is also [[rat|rational]].

steps.title: A longer repeating block
steps.narration: \( \frac{5}{11} = 0.4545\ldots \). The block **45** repeats. Longer block, same rule: it repeats, so it is [[rat|rational]].

steps.title: Never stops, never repeats
steps.narration: \( \sqrt{2} = 1.41421356\ldots \). The digits go on for ever and **no block ever repeats**. That is an [[irr|irrational]] number.

steps.title: Another one: pi
steps.narration: \( \pi = 3.14159265\ldots \) is irrational too: no end, no repeating block.

steps.title: The rule
steps.narration: If the decimal **terminates or recurs**, the number is [[rat|rational]] (it can be written as \( \frac{p}{q} \) with \( q \neq 0 \)). If it does **neither**, it is [[irr|irrational]]. Try the other numbers yourself.

formulas.title: Rational numbers
formulas.text: A rational number can be written as a fraction. Its decimal terminates or recurs.

formulas.title: Irrational numbers
formulas.text: An irrational number cannot be written as p/q. Its decimal never ends and never repeats.

challenges.title: Spot the type
challenges.hint: Look for a block of digits that repeats.
challenges.explain: The block 21 repeats for ever, so the decimal recurs. It is **rational** (it equals 7/33).

challenges.title: Which one is irrational?
challenges.explain: \( \sqrt{3} = 1.7320508\ldots \) never ends and never repeats. The others terminate or recur.

challenges.title: A tricky pattern

options.label: Rational, because there is a pattern

challenges.prompt: \( 0.1010010001\ldots \) (one more 0 each time). Rational or irrational?
challenges.hint: A pattern is not enough: a **fixed block** must repeat.
challenges.explain: The number of zeros keeps growing, so no fixed block repeats. It never ends, so it is **irrational**.

intro: Pick a number and read its decimal. The way the digits behave tells you if it is rational.
takeaways: A pattern like 0.1010010001… is not a repeating block, so it is irrational.

notes.title: Why do rationals repeat?
notes.text: When you divide p by q the remainder can only be one of q possible values, so after at most q steps a remainder comes back and the digits repeat.
